hypotheses.statement: In the retained DSWx-HLS pair, the later products classify fewer AOI cells as water than the earlier products.

evidence_assessments.rationale: The retained WTR counts change 36 to 27 and WTR-2 counts change 135 to 59 on their respective common-valid cells.

hypotheses.scope_limit: Supported only as a change in product class counts; this is not ground-truth water extent.
hypotheses.expected_observation: The retained DSWx-HLS products classify fewer common-valid AOI cells as water in the later product.
hypotheses.would_weaken_if: A recomputation from the retained arrays does not reproduce the reported count changes; this challenges the product-count statement, not ground-truth water extent.
hypotheses.testability_reason: WTR and WTR-2 count changes are available on their respective common-valid centers, with differing valid support.
required_evidence: Retained WTR and WTR-2 arrays and their product validity masks

hypotheses.statement: The optical water-class change explains the measured Sentinel-1-derived backscatter ratio.

evidence_assessments.rationale: The aggregate backscatter ratio measures radar-response change but does not by itself identify a physical cause.

The optical acquisitions are -0.36 and +0.64 days from their corresponding SAR acquisitions. The products use different native grids; exact area-weighted polygon overlap was evaluated without resampling.

At 0.75 common-valid WTR area coverage, 738 SAR cells remain; 710 have at most 0.05 water-fraction change, and the descriptive Pearson r is -0.108. This non-inferential association does not distinguish a water driver; the RTC-S1 pair remains diagnostic.

Across 738 shared cells, the descriptive water-change correlations are -0.108 for VV and -0.078 for VH. Both are weak; the channels share acquisitions and processor and are not independent validation.

hypotheses.scope_limit: No causal attribution; RTC-S1 also lacks a consolidated provider QA verdict.
hypotheses.expected_observation: A quality-valid water transition is spatially associated with the SAR response at suitable temporal and common spatial support.
hypotheses.would_weaken_if: With adequate quality and coverage, valid water observations show no spatial relationship to the SAR response pattern; missing or masked coverage remains inconclusive.
hypotheses.testability_reason: An exact area-weighted common-support overlay was completed; 710 of 738 cells have at most 0.05 water-fraction change, and descriptive Pearson r is -0.108. This does not test the physical explanation. The SAR pair also lacks a consolidated provider QA verdict.
required_evidence: Provider-resolved RTC-S1 product quality for both acquisitions

assessment.summary: The records establish a diagnostic Sentinel-1-derived backscatter ratio and a decline in DSWx-HLS water-class counts over the same WGS84 AOI. An exact area-weighted native-grid overlay was completed. At the 0.75 coverage threshold, 738 cells were retained, 710 had at most 0.05 water-fraction change, and descriptive Pearson r was -0.108. The evidence does not establish a causal explanation or validated flood boundary. A same-pair polarization sensitivity check on 738 shared cells found descriptive water-change correlations of -0.108 (VV) and -0.078 (VH); these related channels do not provide independent validation.

interpretation_limits: OPERA RTC-S1 is Sentinel-1-derived and is not NISAR.
The SAR result remains diagnostic because provider QA metadata contain no consolidated verdict.
DSWx-HLS water classes are optical algorithm outputs, not ground truth.
The two products use different native grids; polygon intersections provide area-weighted descriptive association, not pixel identity or causal evidence.
No event boundary, damage, or physical cause is inferred.
